points: Yirmiyahu promises kol sasson v'kol simcha, weddings, and thanking Hashem in Eretz Yisrael.
Even shepherds shepherding is a bracha. A normal, quiet life, with no more bomb shelters or miluim, is one of the greatest brachos.
Malchus Dovid will return. Hashem's bond with us is as fixed as the sun and moon. Galus and distance from Hashem are unnatural; closeness to Him is our natural state.
He says all this from jail, where Tzidkiyahu put him, and Hashem tells him to buy land in Anasos even as the city is about to fall.
Like the Ponovezher Rav, who lost his family in the Holocaust and bought land for his yeshiva during the war, "dreaming with eyes open," Jews never give up hope and keep building.
